name: Gutenberg Bible, First Major Printed Book
summary: Johannes Gutenberg completes the printing of approximately 180 copies of his Latin Bible, 135 on paper, 45 on vellum, in Mainz. The two-volume Bible uses a typeface designed to resemble hand-lettered manuscripts, initially concealing its mechanical production. The Gutenberg Bible's per-copy cost (approximately 30 florins) is still lower than a manuscript Bible; within decades, mass printing reduces book prices by 80%.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Gutenberg Bible is the first book printed with moveable type in Western Europe; it precipitates an information revolution comparable to the internet: by 1500, over 15 million books are in circulation; the democratization of text access permanently changes how knowledge is produced, transmitted, and challenged; the printing press's role in the Protestant Reformation (distributing Luther's ideas instantly across Europe) makes the Gutenberg Bible the technological ancestor of modern media
